body: A small group of airlines is selling luxury by the seat rather than by the whole aircraft, with all-premium cabins, fewer passengers and private-terminal-style service. The newest entrant is Magnifica Air, a Florida-based United States start-up planning to introduce its Private Class service in 2027, combining spacious Airbus cabins, private airport facilities and personalised hospitality with flights sold by the seat. Magnifica plans to operate Airbus A220-300 and ACJ321neo aircraft with approximately 45 to 54 seats, with two private suites on the A220 and four on the larger A321neo, and it plans to eliminate overhead luggage bins to create a more spacious interior. Passengers would use private airport facilities with dedicated security screening, lounges and transfers, aiming to arrive about 30 minutes before departure, and the product is positioned between commercial first class and private charter, since travellers buy an individual seat instead of hiring an entire aircraft. Magnifica still has work to do before launch, as its aircraft interiors, regulatory approvals and commercial launch remain works in progress.

The market Magnifica is joining already includes all-business-class airlines and semi-private operators with different models. French airline La Compagnie has operated all-business-class transatlantic flights since 2014, using Airbus A321neo aircraft with 76 seats that all convert into fully flat beds on routes connecting Newark with Paris, Milan and seasonal services to Nice, while using commercial airport terminals rather than private facilities. Maldives-based beOnd launched in 2023 with an all-business-class product aimed primarily at luxury leisure travellers, operating Airbus A319 and A321 aircraft with 44 and 68 seats respectively, with lie-flat seating and premium dining, and serving destinations including Zurich, Munich, Milan and Dubai. In the United States, JSX offers public charter flights using regional jets generally configured with around 30 seats, with passengers booking individual seats and using smaller private-terminal facilities, advertising check-in as little as 20 minutes before departure, while Aero offers luxury flights sold by the seat aboard smaller aircraft with premium interiors, targeting affluent leisure travellers flying to selected resort and holiday destinations, particularly in the western United States.

The concept has a difficult history, and that history explains why the current operators look different from one another. In the mid-2000s, Eos Airlines, MAXjet and Silverjet launched premium services, but all three ceased operations between 2007 and 2008, affected by rising fuel prices, financial pressures and competition from larger airlines, while French carrier L'Avion was acquired by British Airways and incorporated into OpenSkies, which subsequently adopted a mixed-cabin model, and British Airways itself operated an all-business-class Airbus A318 service between London City and New York until 2020. Today's operators have adopted different business models: La Compagnie competes for transatlantic business travellers, beOnd targets luxury holidaymakers, and JSX and Aero concentrate on convenience, smaller airports and private-aviation-style service. All face the same basic financial challenge, since aircraft with fewer seats must generate sufficient revenue per passenger to cover operating costs, and they compete with established airlines investing in private business-class suites, improved lounges and premium onboard services, while serving fewer routes than their larger commercial counterparts.
en.summary: Magnifica Air plans to join La Compagnie, beOnd, JSX and Aero in the all-premium market in 2027, selling luxury seats on small Airbus cabins with private-terminal-style service, in a segment whose earlier carriers mostly failed in 2007 and 2008.
en.title: The world's all-premium airlines: Magnifica, La Compagnie, beOnd and the seat-by-seat luxury market

body: 一小群航空公司正在以座位為單位販售奢華體驗，而非整架包機：全高級客艙、較少旅客，以及類似私人航廈的服務。最新加入者是美國佛羅里達新創公司Magnifica Air，計畫於2027年推出Private Class服務，結合寬敞的空中巴士客艙、私人機場設施與個人化款待，並以座位為單位售票。Magnifica Air計畫營運空中巴士A220-300與ACJ321neo，座位數約45至54席，A220設有2間私人套房，較大的A321neo則有4間，並計畫取消頭頂行李櫃以營造更寬敞的機艙。旅客將使用私人機場設施，享有專屬安檢、貴賓室與接送服務，目標是起飛前約30分鐘抵達；產品定位介於商業頭等艙與私人包機之間，因為旅客購買的是單一座位，而非整架飛機。不過Magnifica Air在啟航前仍有工作要完成，機艙內裝、法規核准與商業啟動都還在進行中。

Magnifica Air將加入的市場，已經有全商務艙航空公司與半私人業者，各自採取不同模式。法國航空公司La Compagnie自2014年起營運全商務艙跨大西洋航班，使用76席空中巴士A321neo，全數座位皆可轉換為全平躺睡床，航線連接紐華克與巴黎、米蘭及季節性的尼斯，並使用商業機場航廈而非私人設施。馬爾地夫航空公司beOnd於2023年推出，主要鎖定奢華休閒旅客，營運空中巴士A319與A321，座位數分別為44席與68席，配備平躺座椅與高級餐飲，目的地包括蘇黎世、慕尼黑、米蘭與杜拜。美國業者JSX則提供公共包機航班，使用一般配置約30席的區域噴射機，旅客以座位為單位訂票並使用較小的私人航廈設施，標榜最短20分鐘前報到；而Aero則以座位為單位販售奢華航班，使用配備高級內裝的小型飛機，主要鎖定前往美國西部精選度假與假日目的地的富裕休閒旅客。

這個概念有過艱難的歷史，也正因如此，今日業者的樣貌各不相同。2000年代中期，Eos Airlines、MAXjet與Silverjet推出高級服務，但三家皆於2007年至2008年間停業，受到燃油價格上漲、財務壓力與大型航空公司競爭影響；法國全商務艙業者L'Avion則被英國航空收購並併入OpenSkies，後者隨後改採混合客艙模式，而英國航空本身營運的全商務艙空中巴士A318倫敦城市機場至紐約航線則持續至2020年。今日業者採取不同商業模式：La Compagnie爭取跨大西洋商務旅客，beOnd鎖定奢華度假客，JSX與Aero則著重便利性、較小機場與私人航空式服務。但所有業者都面臨相同的基本財務挑戰：座位較少的飛機必須從每位旅客身上創造足夠收入以支應營運成本，同時還要與大力投資私人商務艙套房、升級貴賓室與高級機上服務的傳統航空公司競爭，而且航線也比大型商業航空公司少。
zh.summary: Magnifica Air計畫於2027年加入La Compagnie、beOnd、JSX與Aero所在的全高級市場，以小型空中巴士客艙與私人航廈式服務按座位販售奢華體驗；這個市場的早期業者多半已於2007年至2008年間停業。
zh.title: 全球全高級航空公司：Magnifica、La Compagnie、beOnd與按座位販售的奢華市場
